binding.p: Modern binding. Brown leather over wooden boards. 3 double raised bands and endbands. Originally, two brass clasps. , stamped in gold: A 184.

decoNote.p: Simple tooling consisting of a double frame and some and triangular shapes ending in silver floral shape by the bands.

origin.p: Germany , 15th century. The manuscript was likely made for a Dominican monastery, perhaps St Gertrud's in Cologne. The manuscript contains an office for both St Dominic and St Gertrud, and mentions a chuch of St Gertrud on . Both saints are also given prominence in the two litanies (, , ). The long list of female saints in the litanies (, ) and the instructions for sisters, on e.g. , gives further support for a nunnery as place of origin. However, the decoration may favour an origin in the eastern part of the Dutch region.
The mention of two Katherina in the litany indicates that one of them should be Catherina of Siena, who was canonized in . This may give a terminus post quem for the manuscript.

provenance.p: On there are two notes by previous owners from the 17th century: Soror Maria Elisabetha Monica Hansen and Soror Maria Anna Rosa Gesser, sisters in a Dominican convent (prediger ordens). It is possible that the manuscript remained at St Gertrud's until the secularisation around 1800. Later In the 19th century, the manuscript belonged to Bernhard Rosenblad (see note on ). It was purchased from him by G. J. R. Gordon.

acquisition.p: Purchased from G. J. R. Gordon by the National Library of Sweden in .

summary.p: The manuscript consists of two separate parts (Unit 1 and Unit 2) with two different styles of decoration. The first part (offices) contains the major part, and the second part (antiphonary) contains musical notation and is less decorated than the first, but by a more skilled illuminator. The difference between the illuminators is clearly seen when comparing the precision in the lines and the distribution of the gold. The latter part might be of a slightly later date than the first.

decoNote.p: These four inititals have marginal borders of flowers (lilies, columbines etc), berries and oak- and acanthus leaves. The initial is placed on a golden field with concave corners. The letter is painted in blue with white highlights. The letters are filled by stylized six- or three-lobed flowers and leaves in gold, green, rose, red, blue, violet, and orange.
: plain initial over 4 lines in blue, inner space decorated in red and blue.
: plain initials over 1-3 lines in red and blue. Some of the initials are decorated with stylised flowers in red and blue ink, e.g. on or .

note.p: Begins with Purification of the Blessed Virgin Mary (31 Jan), and ends with the Assumption of the Virgin Mary (15 Aug.)

layout.note: The basic layout for the music consists of four groups of four staves each, ruled in red ink. Guidelines in lead.

musicNotation.p: Black square notation on a four-line red staff. Sometimes word division lines. Additions of incipit markings (double vertical strokes).

decoNote.p: : opening puzzle initial over 8 staves in blue and gold with embellishments of thin lines of pen-work in red and violet, and fillings in green with red and violet contours. The letter also has marginal stems in the same kind of pen-work, filling the inner margin, in an angular design where the horizontals and verticals are emphasized.
: cadels over 4 staves and 1 line in black with details in red.
: plain initals over 4 staves and 1 line alternating in red and blue, often with complex flourishing in the same style as the opening initial.
